title: Records Management
topics: Nature of records and records management

items.q: The statement “a code given to one record so that it can be told apart from every other” describes which of the following?
o: Unique identifier
Version control
Metadata
File plan
items.s: Unique identifier is a code given to one record so that it can be told apart from every other.

items.q: Which term is described by “the written steps for salvaging material damaged by fire, flood or other harm”?
o: Compliance audit
Benchmarking
Vital records
Disaster plan
items.s: Disaster plan is the written steps for salvaging material damaged by fire, flood or other harm.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Checksum.
o: the duty not to pass on what was received in confidence
a timetable that authorises the destruction or transfer of classes once their period has run
the permanently valuable records of a person or body, kept for reference by others
a computed value used to detect whether a file has altered in storage
items.s: Checksum: a computed value used to detect whether a file has altered in storage. The other options describe Archive, Confidentiality, Disposal schedule.

items.q: The statement “the act of lodging a record in a system so that it is registered, described and controlled” describes which of the following?
o: File plan
Registration
Unique identifier
Capture
items.s: Capture is the act of lodging a record in a system so that it is registered, described and controlled.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Evidential value.
o: the usefulness of material in showing how and why a decision was reached
the legal right of members of the public to ask for and receive official records
the entry of a record in a log with a number and a date so that it can be traced
the act of lodging a record in a system so that it is registered, described and controlled
items.s: Evidential value: the usefulness of material in showing how and why a decision was reached. The other options describe Capture, Freedom of information, Registration.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Disposal schedule?
o: a timetable that authorises the destruction or transfer of classes once their period has run
the judgement of how long material is needed and whether it deserves permanent keeping
the worth of material to later researchers for evidence or for information
an agreed published specification against which practice can be measured
items.s: Disposal schedule: a timetable that authorises the destruction or transfer of classes once their period has run. The other options describe Appraisal, Standard, Secondary value.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Correspondence file?
o: a folder holding the letters and memoranda on one matter in the order they were received
a single case folder containing both paper and machine readable parts
the cutting of paper into strips or particles so that its content cannot be read
a page on which each officer records the action taken on a piece of correspondence
items.s: Correspondence file: a folder holding the letters and memoranda on one matter in the order they were received. The other options describe Minute sheet, Shredding, Hybrid file.
items.t: Nature of records and records management

items.q: The statement “information created or received in the course of business and kept as proof of that business” describes which of the following?
o: Record
Records centre
Recordkeeping
Archive
items.s: Record is information created or received in the course of business and kept as proof of that business.
items.t: Nature of records and records management

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Exemption.
o: a stated category of material that may lawfully be withheld from disclosure
a plan showing the functions and activities of a body and the records each produces
the small set of items a body must have to continue working after a disaster
the written steps for salvaging material damaged by fire, flood or other harm
items.s: Exemption: a stated category of material that may lawfully be withheld from disclosure. The other options describe Disaster plan, Classification scheme, Vital records.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Certificate of destruction.
o: a signed statement naming what was destroyed, when and by whose authority
any carrier of written or graphic content, whether or not it serves as evidence of an activity
the keeping of all of an organisation's papers in one place under one control
the act of lodging a record in a system so that it is registered, described and controlled
items.s: Certificate of destruction: a signed statement naming what was destroyed, when and by whose authority. The other options describe Document, Capture, Centralised filing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Primary value.
o: software that stores, tracks and retrieves an organisation's word processed items and scanned images
the stage at which a record is first made or received and set into a system
the irreversible removal of material once its authorised period has ended
the worth of material to the body that created it for its own continuing business
items.s: Primary value: the worth of material to the body that created it for its own continuing business. The other options describe Electronic document management system, Creation, Destruction.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Conservation?
o: work that repairs damage and slows decay without altering what the item says
the formal recording of material as it enters the permanent custody of an institution
a signed statement naming what was destroyed, when and by whose authority
material created, held and used in machine readable form as evidence of an activity
items.s: Conservation: work that repairs damage and slows decay without altering what the item says. The other options describe Accessioning, Electronic record, Certificate of destruction.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Vital records?
o: the small set of items a body must have to continue working after a disaster
a group of items arranged under one system of numbering because they share a function or form
the legal right of members of the public to ask for and receive official records
the duty not to pass on what was received in confidence
items.s: Vital records: the small set of items a body must have to continue working after a disaster. The other options describe Series, Freedom of information, Confidentiality.

items.q: Confidentiality may be defined as
o: the duty not to pass on what was received in confidence
the keeping of all of an organisation's papers in one place under one control
a folder holding the letters and memoranda on one matter in the order they were received
software that stores, tracks and retrieves an organisation's word processed items and scanned images
items.s: Confidentiality: the duty not to pass on what was received in confidence. The other options describe Electronic document management system, Correspondence file, Centralised filing.

items.q: The statement “the arrangements prepared in advance for carrying on after a disruption” describes which of the following?
o: Standard
Policy statement
Business continuity plan
Disaster plan
items.s: Business continuity plan is the arrangements prepared in advance for carrying on after a disruption.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Informational value?
o: the whole body of material made or received by one creator in the course of its work
software that stores, tracks and retrieves an organisation's word processed items and scanned images
the formal recording of material as it enters the permanent custody of an institution
the usefulness of material for the facts it holds about people, places or events
items.s: Informational value: the usefulness of material for the facts it holds about people, places or events. The other options describe Fonds, Accessioning, Electronic document management system.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Deaccessioning?
o: material still in frequent use for the activity that produced it
the formal removal of an item from the permanent collection with a written reason
a page on which each officer records the action taken on a piece of correspondence
the occurrence, such as a case closing, that starts the count of a retention period
items.s: Deaccessioning: the formal removal of an item from the permanent collection with a written reason. The other options describe Current record, Trigger event, Minute sheet.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Chronological filing.
o: an instruction that stops disposal because of litigation, audit or inquiry
arrangement of folders by the letters of names or subjects
the whole body of material made or received by one creator in the course of its work
arrangement of papers in the order of their dates
items.s: Chronological filing: arrangement of papers in the order of their dates. The other options describe Alphabetic filing, Legal hold, Fonds.

items.q: Which term is described by “the documented record of every person who has held an item, used to show it is untampered”?
o: Exemption
Authenticity
Confidentiality
Chain of custody
items.s: Chain of custody is the documented record of every person who has held an item, used to show it is untampered.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Semi-current record?
o: arrangement of papers in the order of their dates
material no longer needed for daily work but still required occasionally for reference
the whole body of material made or received by one creator in the course of its work
the everyday making and keeping of the evidence a body needs in order to work and account for itself
items.s: Semi-current record: material no longer needed for daily work but still required occasionally for reference. The other options describe Recordkeeping, Chronological filing, Fonds.

items.q: Which term is described by “the copying of stored files onto fresh media before the old media fail”?
o: Digital obsolescence
Enterprise content management
Checksum
Refreshment
items.s: Refreshment is the copying of stored files onto fresh media before the old media fail.

items.q: Which term is described by “arrangement of folders by assigned numbers, with an index to names”?
o: Centralised filing
Numeric filing
Alphabetic filing
Decentralised filing
items.s: Numeric filing is arrangement of folders by assigned numbers, with an index to names.

items.q: Which term is described by “the book or database in which received correspondence is listed on arrival”?
o: Outward register
Minute sheet
Inward register
Centralised filing
items.s: Inward register is the book or database in which received correspondence is listed on arrival.

items.q: Which term is described by “the rule that material must be kept in the group of its creator and not mixed with others”?
o: Provenance
Fonds
Finding aid
Encapsulation
items.s: Provenance is the rule that material must be kept in the group of its creator and not mixed with others.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Standard.
o: a signed statement naming what was destroyed, when and by whose authority
a written description of a collection that allows its contents to be traced
the sealing of a fragile sheet between transparent films for handling without damage
an agreed published specification against which practice can be measured
items.s: Standard: an agreed published specification against which practice can be measured. The other options describe Encapsulation, Finding aid, Certificate of destruction.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Records manager?
o: a body charged with collecting, caring for and making available the permanently valuable records of an area or an organisation
the loss of the ability to read material because the hardware or software that made it is gone
the officer who plans and runs the system by which a body keeps its evidence
a short formal declaration of what an organisation undertakes to do about its records
items.s: Records manager: the officer who plans and runs the system by which a body keeps its evidence. The other options describe Policy statement, Digital obsolescence, Archival institution.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Numeric filing?
o: arrangement of folders by assigned numbers, with an index to names
the sequence of stages a record passes through from its making to its final fate
the rule that the arrangement given by the creating office must be left undisturbed
arrangement of folders by the letters of names or subjects
items.s: Numeric filing: arrangement of folders by assigned numbers, with an index to names. The other options describe Original order, Life cycle, Alphabetic filing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Retention schedule.
o: the systematic examination of the holdings of an office to establish their volume and condition
a list fixing how long each class of material must be held before disposal
an agreed pattern for labelling files so that their content can be read from the name
a plan showing the functions and activities of a body and the records each produces
items.s: Retention schedule: a list fixing how long each class of material must be held before disposal. The other options describe Naming convention, Records survey, Classification scheme.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Current record?
o: material still in frequent use for the activity that produced it
the range of final actions taken on records, namely destruction, transfer or continued holding
the act of lodging a record in a system so that it is registered, described and controlled
software that stores, tracks and retrieves an organisation's word processed items and scanned images
items.s: Current record: material still in frequent use for the activity that produced it. The other options describe Disposition, Electronic document management system, Capture.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Unique identifier?
o: the range of final actions taken on records, namely destruction, transfer or continued holding
the copying of stored files onto fresh media before the old media fail
an approach that treats the making, keeping and use of evidence as overlapping concerns rather than fixed stages
a code given to one record so that it can be told apart from every other
items.s: Unique identifier: a code given to one record so that it can be told apart from every other. The other options describe Refreshment, Disposition, Continuum model.

items.q: Data protection may be defined as
o: the body of rules governing how personal details may be collected, held and shared
the act of lodging a record in a system so that it is registered, described and controlled
the documented record of every person who has held an item, used to show it is untampered
the permanently valuable records of a person or body, kept for reference by others
items.s: Data protection: the body of rules governing how personal details may be collected, held and shared. The other options describe Archive, Chain of custody, Capture.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Business continuity plan?
o: the keeping of all of an organisation's papers in one place under one control
the legal right of members of the public to ask for and receive official records
the arrangements prepared in advance for carrying on after a disruption
the practice of tracking which copy of a document is the current one
items.s: Business continuity plan: the arrangements prepared in advance for carrying on after a disruption. The other options describe Freedom of information, Centralised filing, Version control.

items.q: The statement “the small set of items a body must have to continue working after a disaster” describes which of the following?
o: Records manager
Vital records
Disaster plan
Staff training
items.s: Vital records is the small set of items a body must have to continue working after a disaster.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Vital records.
o: the body of rules governing how personal details may be collected, held and shared
any detail by which one living individual can be identified
the small set of items a body must have to continue working after a disaster
the loss of the ability to read material because the hardware or software that made it is gone
items.s: Vital records: the small set of items a body must have to continue working after a disaster. The other options describe Data protection, Digital obsolescence, Personal data.

items.q: All of the following belong to Access, privacy and legal duties EXCEPT
o: Access policy
Freedom of information
Exemption
Provenance
items.s: Every other option belongs to Access, privacy and legal duties. “Provenance” belongs to Archival transfer and preservation, not Access, privacy and legal duties.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines File plan.
o: structured data about a record that describes its content, context and management history
an arrangement that fixes where each group of related material is to be kept
the keeping of all of an organisation's papers in one place under one control
the written steps for salvaging material damaged by fire, flood or other harm
items.s: File plan: an arrangement that fixes where each group of related material is to be kept. The other options describe Metadata, Centralised filing, Disaster plan.

items.q: The statement “the keeping of all of an organisation's papers in one place under one control” describes which of the following?
o: Decentralised filing
Centralised filing
Alphabetic filing
Outward register
items.s: Centralised filing is the keeping of all of an organisation's papers in one place under one control.

items.q: Which term is described by “work that repairs damage and slows decay without altering what the item says”?
o: Conservation
Original order
Provenance
Series
items.s: Conservation is work that repairs damage and slows decay without altering what the item says.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Enterprise content management?
o: a system that handles an organisation's documents, images and records together with their workflows
the entry of a record in a log with a number and a date so that it can be traced
a check that actual practice matches the rules and schedules laid down
the moving of material to a records centre or an archival institution
items.s: Enterprise content management: a system that handles an organisation's documents, images and records together with their workflows. The other options describe Compliance audit, Registration, Transfer.

items.q: Which term is described by “a list fixing how long each class of material must be held before disposal”?
o: Disposal schedule
Retention schedule
Sampling
Primary value
items.s: Retention schedule is a list fixing how long each class of material must be held before disposal.

items.q: The statement “an approach that treats the making, keeping and use of evidence as overlapping concerns rather than fixed stages” describes which of the following?
o: Continuum model
Semi-current record
Non-current record
Records survey
items.s: Continuum model is an approach that treats the making, keeping and use of evidence as overlapping concerns rather than fixed stages.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Finding aid?
o: a folder holding the letters and memoranda on one matter in the order they were received
the formal recording of material as it enters the permanent custody of an institution
the irreversible removal of material once its authorised period has ended
a written description of a collection that allows its contents to be traced
items.s: Finding aid: a written description of a collection that allows its contents to be traced. The other options describe Correspondence file, Accessioning, Destruction.

items.q: All of the following belong to Creation, capture and classification EXCEPT
o: Capture
Semi-current record
Registration
Classification scheme
items.s: Every other option belongs to Creation, capture and classification. “Semi-current record” belongs to Records life cycle and continuum, not Creation, capture and classification.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Enterprise content management?
o: a code given to one record so that it can be told apart from every other
a group of items arranged under one system of numbering because they share a function or form
the arrangements prepared in advance for carrying on after a disruption
a system that handles an organisation's documents, images and records together with their workflows
items.s: Enterprise content management: a system that handles an organisation's documents, images and records together with their workflows. The other options describe Business continuity plan, Unique identifier, Series.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Encapsulation?
o: the copying of stored files onto fresh media before the old media fail
a written set of rules stating who may see which material and under what conditions
the sealing of a fragile sheet between transparent films for handling without damage
the office where incoming and outgoing correspondence is received, registered and filed
items.s: Encapsulation: the sealing of a fragile sheet between transparent films for handling without damage. The other options describe Refreshment, Access policy, Registry.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Disposition.
o: the range of final actions taken on records, namely destruction, transfer or continued holding
a body charged with collecting, caring for and making available the permanently valuable records of an area or an organisation
a page on which each officer records the action taken on a piece of correspondence
the book or database in which received correspondence is listed on arrival
items.s: Disposition: the range of final actions taken on records, namely destruction, transfer or continued holding. The other options describe Archival institution, Minute sheet, Inward register.

items.q: The statement “the irreversible removal of material once its authorised period has ended” describes which of the following?
o: Transfer
Destruction
Deaccessioning
Certificate of destruction
items.s: Destruction is the irreversible removal of material once its authorised period has ended.

the judgement of how long material is needed and whether it deserves permanent keeping
material created, held and used in machine readable form as evidence of an activity
the book or database in which received correspondence is listed on arrival
items.s: Appraisal: the judgement of how long material is needed and whether it deserves permanent keeping. The other options describe Inward register, Electronic record, Vital records.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Inward register?
o: the comparison of one programme with the practice of comparable bodies elsewhere
the book or database in which received correspondence is listed on arrival
the entry of a record in a log with a number and a date so that it can be traced
an instruction that stops disposal because of litigation, audit or inquiry
items.s: Inward register: the book or database in which received correspondence is listed on arrival. The other options describe Benchmarking, Legal hold, Registration.

items.q: Disposition may be defined as
o: a check that actual practice matches the rules and schedules laid down
the field concerned with the efficient and systematic control of the evidence a body creates, from its making to its final fate
the range of final actions taken on records, namely destruction, transfer or continued holding
the usefulness of material for the facts it holds about people, places or events
items.s: Disposition: the range of final actions taken on records, namely destruction, transfer or continued holding. The other options describe Informational value, Compliance audit, Records management.

items.q: Version control may be defined as
o: the systematic examination of the holdings of an office to establish their volume and condition
the usefulness of material for the facts it holds about people, places or events
the practice of tracking which copy of a document is the current one
the keeping of a representative portion of a large series and the destroying of the rest
items.s: Version control: the practice of tracking which copy of a document is the current one. The other options describe Records survey, Informational value, Sampling.

items.q: The statement “an agreed published specification against which practice can be measured” describes which of the following?
o: Staff training
Compliance audit
Vital records
Standard
items.s: Standard is an agreed published specification against which practice can be measured.

items.q: Preservation may be defined as
o: material no longer needed in the office at all and awaiting a decision on its fate
the practice of tracking which copy of a document is the current one
the whole set of measures, including storage and handling, that keep material usable
the field concerned with the efficient and systematic control of the evidence a body creates, from its making to its final fate
items.s: Preservation: the whole set of measures, including storage and handling, that keep material usable. The other options describe Version control, Non-current record, Records management.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Trigger event.
o: a short formal declaration of what an organisation undertakes to do about its records
an instruction that stops disposal because of litigation, audit or inquiry
the keeping of papers by the unit that creates them rather than in one registry
the occurrence, such as a case closing, that starts the count of a retention period
items.s: Trigger event: the occurrence, such as a case closing, that starts the count of a retention period. The other options describe Legal hold, Policy statement, Decentralised filing.

a body charged with collecting, caring for and making available the permanently valuable records of an area or an organisation
the body of rules governing how personal details may be collected, held and shared
a page on which each officer records the action taken on a piece of correspondence
items.s: Archival institution: a body charged with collecting, caring for and making available the permanently valuable records of an area or an organisation. The other options describe Data protection, Minute sheet, Disposition.

o: the arrangements prepared in advance for carrying on after a disruption
the usefulness of material for the facts it holds about people, places or events
the formal removal of an item from the permanent collection with a written reason

items.q: Recordkeeping may be defined as
o: the sealing of a fragile sheet between transparent films for handling without damage
the everyday making and keeping of the evidence a body needs in order to work and account for itself
the quality of being what it claims to be, made and sent by the party named
material still in frequent use for the activity that produced it
items.s: Recordkeeping: the everyday making and keeping of the evidence a body needs in order to work and account for itself. The other options describe Authenticity, Current record, Encapsulation.

the instruction given to employees so that they file and dispose of material correctly
a stated category of material that may lawfully be withheld from disclosure

the moving of material to a records centre or an archival institution
arrangement of papers in the order of their dates
the worth of material to the body that created it for its own continuing business
items.s: Transfer: the moving of material to a records centre or an archival institution. The other options describe Primary value, Chronological filing, Record.

Chronological filing
